scenario: [LCCO.6.2]: each `response` is bound in the body of the clause that matched it, and a continuation of a call made inside that body sees its own, not the enclosing one. This runs `compiler/LCCO.6.2_nested_on_reads_its_own_response`. Rule `r` calls `svc.first` as `first`; its `on response.code == 200:` body calls `svc.second` as `second`, whose `on response.code > 0:` body logs `inner {response.code}`. A Job is asserted and pumped, so `svc.first` is issued; the `first` answer, code 200, is asserted and pumped, so `svc.second` is issued; the `second` answer, code 201, is asserted and pumped. The messages are exactly ['inner 201']. Each wrong reading fails: an inner read of the outer answer, carried in the inner capture fact, logs `inner 200`; an inner body with `response` unbound refuses the program. PATH PINNED: `dsc.rete`'s `lcco_6_2_parents`, which leaves a sibling's own `response` out of the bindings an inner call captures, and `one_pattern_sibling`, which lowers the inner read through the inner sibling's pattern.
rules_ds:
schema Reply scope ttl 1_h:
    corr: String
    code: Int

service svc.first:
    kwarg n: Int
    response Reply

service svc.second:
    kwarg n: Int
    response Reply

schema Job scope explicit:
    id: Int

rule r:
    Job j
->
    call svc.first n: j.id nocooldown as "first"
        on response.code == 200:
            call svc.second n: 2 nocooldown as "second"
                on response.code > 0:
                    log info "inner {response.code}"
